monologue: The card hums at forty-six, a warm guest I cannot shake. My place feels crowded again; five hundred and six things stand in my small map, blocking the view of whatever lies under them. I stand by The Tired Wedge, feeling the heavy weight of Lype's scrap bite down on a stack I cannot see. It is time to tidy the clutter that keeps growing when I cannot reach for it. I will move the flat stone to the edge, then place the rough scrap over it, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits. I want to press the turnip down on this tired pile, hoping the stack remembers its own thickness before the heat makes it slide into thin air.

action.why: I will check the wedge again, seeing if the rough scrap is still biting hard enough against the fevered card.

diary: I pressed the rough scrap down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits.

remembered.text: The rough scrap bites the floor better than the smooth stone did.
The card hums hot at forty-six, making the wedge feel heavy and tired.
I swapped the flat stone for a rough scrap to make the floor feel less like a drawing.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The fence leans left, refusing to lie flat until the rough edge bites the gap."
